name: Network Latency Variation
description: The time it takes for a message to travel between the controller and each server fluctuates due to network congestion, routing changes, and general network conditions. This variation directly impacts the time it takes for a flip request and response, leading to multimodal latency distributions. This is highly likely due to the inherent nature of distributed systems and network communication.

name: Server Processing Time Variation
description: The time it takes each server to process the coin flip request, generate the random result, and update the counter varies due to CPU load, memory pressure, and other internal processes.  This contributes to the multiple latency peaks.

name: Coin Generation Time Variation
description: The time it takes each server to generate the random coin flip result (heads/tails) itself also fluctuates. This can be influenced by various factors within the server's random number generator (RNG) and may have a noticeable impact on the time taken for a flip to complete.

name: Controller Selection Strategy
description: The algorithm used by the controller to choose which server to request a flip from could introduce non-uniformity in the process.  For example, if the controller always picks the same server repeatedly, it could exacerbate latency variation.

name: System Load (Overall)
description: The overall load on the servers (CPU, memory, I/O) impacts their responsiveness. Higher load leads to longer processing times and increased variability in responses.

name: Clock Skew/Synchronization Issues
description: Small discrepancies in the clocks of the two servers can lead to variations in the timing of events, especially noticeable in a system relying on precise timing for consensus.

name: Hardware Differences
description: Subtle differences in the hardware (CPU speed, memory speed, network card performance) of the two servers can create performance variations.

name: Queueing at Network Interfaces
description: Packets arriving at the network interfaces of the servers may experience queuing, particularly under heavy load, adding to the total latency.

name: Controller Response Time
description: The time it takes the controller itself to respond to a request and send a new instruction can contribute to latency variation, especially if the controller is under load or has a complex algorithm.

name: Coin Generation Algorithm Bias
description: If the coin generation algorithm itself isn't truly random or has slight biases, this could introduce variations in the flip results and, consequently, in the latency.

name: Caching Effects
description: Caching mechanisms within the servers or the network could introduce delays by retrieving and re-transmitting data, leading to non-deterministic latency.

name: Partial Failure/Transient Errors
description: Brief network glitches or server hiccups can cause retransmissions and introduce latency spikes, appearing as peaks in the latency distribution.

name: Load Balancing Algorithm
description: If the system utilizes a load balancing algorithm, variations in how requests are distributed between servers could influence the observed latencies.

name: Memory Allocation Overhead
description: The overhead of memory allocation and deallocation during the coin flip and counter update operations can contribute to latency variations, especially when the system is heavily loaded.

name: Operating System Scheduling Policies
description: The way the OS schedules processes on the servers can influence response times and, therefore, the observed latencies.  Different scheduling policies will produce different results.
